drivingQuestion: How can Rabbi have hung his tefillin if hanging them is condemned?
outcomeNote: Two reconciliations offered; the second is justified by what the report teaches.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: אֲנִי רָאִיתִי אֶת רַבִּי שֶׁתָּלָה תְּפִילָּיו. מֵיתִיבִי: הַתּוֹלֶה תְּפִילָּיו יִתָּלוּ לוֹ חַיָּיו!
segments.en: The Gemara resumes its discussion of phylacteries. «Rabbi Ḥanina said: I saw Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi «hang his phylacteries.» The Gemara «raises an objection:» It was taught in a baraita that «one who hangs his phylacteries will have his life hang» in the balance.

segments.he: דּוֹרְשֵׁי חֲמוּרוֹת אָמְרוּ: ״וְהָיוּ חַיֶּיךָ תְּלֻאִים לְךָ מִנֶּגֶד״, זֶה הַתּוֹלֶה תְּפִילָּיו.
segments.en: Moreover, «the Symbolic Interpreters» of the Torah «said» that the verse: «“And your life shall hang in doubt before you [minneged]”» (Deuteronomy 28:66), that is the punishment of «one who hangs his phylacteries.»

segments.he: לָא קַשְׁיָא הָא בִּרְצוּעָה. הָא בִּקְצִיצָה.
segments.en: The Gemara replies: This apparent contradiction «is not difficult, as this» baraita, which condemns one who hangs his phylacteries, refers to one who hangs them «by the strap,» allowing the leather boxes into which the parchment is placed to dangle in a deprecating way, which is certainly prohibited. «That» baraita, which relates that Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi would hang his phylacteries and that it is clearly permitted, refers to when one hangs them «from the box» with the straps dangling.

segments.he: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לָא שְׁנָא רְצוּעָה וְלָא שְׁנָא קְצִיצָה — אָסוּר. וְכִי תְּלָה רַבִּי — בְּכִיסְתָּא תְּלָה.
segments.en: «And if you wish, say» another explanation instead: «There is no difference» whether he hangs the phylacteries from the «strap and there is no difference» whether he hangs the phylacteries from «the box;» both «are prohibited. And when Rabbi» Yehuda HaNasi «hung» his phylacteries, «he hung them in» their «pouch.»

segments.he: אִי הָכִי מַאי לְמֵימְרָא? מַהוּ דְתֵימָא תִּיבְעֵי הַנָּחָה כְּסֵפֶר תּוֹרָה — קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «If so, what» is the purpose «to relate» that incident? The Gemara replies: «Lest you say» that phylacteries «would require placement» atop a surface, «as» is the custom with «a Torah scroll.» Therefore, «it teaches us» that this is unnecessary.
